name: pairdrop
description: Local file sharing between devices through a web browser

fields.name: PAIRDROP_PORT
fields.label: R1: App Port
fields.help: Host port used to open PairDrop in your browser.

fields.name: PUID
fields.label: R2: PUID
fields.help:
Linux user ID used by the container.
Use the ID of the account that should own files created by PairDrop.

fields.name: PGID
fields.label: R3: PGID
fields.help:
Linux group ID used by the container.
Use the group ID associated with the selected PUID.

fields.name: TZ
fields.label: R4: Timezone
fields.help:
Timezone used by PairDrop logs.
Example: Asia/Dubai or Etc/UTC.

fields.name: WS_FALLBACK
fields.label: O1: WebSocket Fallback
fields.help:
Enable this when peer-to-peer WebRTC is unavailable, such as through some VPNs.
Fallback transfers pass through the server and use its bandwidth.

fields.name: RATE_LIMIT
fields.label: O2: Rate Limit
fields.help: Enable to limit each client to 100 requests per five minutes.

fields.name: RTC_CONFIG
fields.label: O3: Custom RTC Config Path
fields.help:
Optional path inside the container to a JSON file containing custom STUN or TURN server settings.
Leave blank to use PairDrop defaults.

fields.name: DEBUG_MODE
fields.label: O4: Debug Mode
fields.help:
Logs client IP addresses for HTTP server debugging.
Do not enable this in production.

fields.name: RESTART_POLICY
fields.label: O5: Restart Policy
fields.help: Controls whether the container restarts automatically.

fields.name: PAIRDROP_IMAGE
fields.label: A1: Image
fields.help:
Docker image used for PairDrop.
Change this only if you want a different tag or image source.

fields.name: PAIRDROP_CONTAINER_NAME
fields.label: Container Name
fields.help: EasyDocker sets the container name from the project name.

ui.overview: PairDrop lets devices send files and text to each other directly from a web browser, similar to AirDrop but across platforms.
what_happens: A PairDrop container will be created using the LinuxServer image
The PairDrop web interface will be published on host port 3000 by default
PUID, PGID, and timezone will be passed into the container
WebSocket fallback, rate limiting, custom RTC configuration, and debug logging can be configured under Optional
No persistent volume is required for the standard PairDrop setup
ui.data_location: PairDrop does not require persistent application storage for its standard configuration.
